backlog.spec: After featurizing, compute on the training matrix the descriptor columns' absolute pairwise correlations. Drop one of each pair with |r|>0.95 and drop constant columns. Apply the same column mask to the test features. Keep the Morgan block intact.
backlog.title: Drop correlated descriptors

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, hold out about 20% of the training molecules as an inner split grouped by Murcko scaffold (sklearn GroupShuffleSplit with groups from MurckoScaffoldSmiles, random_state=seed). Train LightGBM and CatBoost with a large n_estimators/iterations budget (for example 1500 at learning_rate=0.03) and early-stopping on the inner held-out split using AUC. Refit on the full training data with the best iteration count found. The RF and rank average are unchanged.
backlog.title: Per-member iteration count chosen by an inner scaffold split

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, standardize each SMILES first: parse, keep the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser), neutralize with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger, fall back to the original mol on failure. Use the cleaned mol for featurize. Add two more rank-averaged members: a Tanimoto kNN (k=10, similarity-weighted votes) on binary Morgan bits, and an MLPClassifier (hidden 256,64, early_stopping, alpha 1e-3) on QuantileTransformer-scaled descriptors, averaged over 3 seeds. Final is the equal-weight rank mean of all five members.
backlog.title: Standardize + kNN + MLP combined base

backlog.spec: Test whether the random forest is dead weight now that two gradient boosters are present. Remove the RandomForestClassifier member entirely and return the rank-average of just LightGBM and CatBoost, with their current hyperparameters and the current feature matrix (RDKit descriptors plus 2048-bit radius-2 Morgan counts). Delete the now-unused RF settings constants and import so the file stays clean. This is a cheap ablation that also roughly halves the fit cost, freeing runtime for later ideas if it comes out neutral.
backlog.title: Drop the random forest from the ensemble

backlog.spec: Change only the LGBMClassifier in fit_predict to boosting_type='dart' with drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, n_estimators=300, learning_rate=0.1, num_leaves=31, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.3, n_jobs=8 and random_state=seed. Dart is a LightGBM booster type, not the XGBoost dart already tried. The RF and CatBoost members and the rank average stay the same.
backlog.title: LightGBM as a dart booster

backlog.spec: In featurize(), compute the generic Murcko scaffold (MurckoScaffold.MakeScaffoldGeneric on MurckoScaffold.GetScaffoldForMol(m)) for each molecule. Build a fixed-length count vector over the 512 generic scaffold SMILES with the highest training frequency (vocabulary fixed inside fit_predict from the training molecules), plus a count of ring systems and the number of rings in the scaffold. Append these columns to the descriptor and Morgan features; the models are unchanged.
backlog.title: Generic Murcko scaffold count features

backlog.spec: Replace the final rank-average in fit_predict with a geometric mean of the three members' predicted probabilities. Concretely, clip each member's predict_proba[:,1] to [1e-6, 1-1e-6], take the mean of the log-odds across the three members, and return the sigmoid of that mean. The models themselves are unchanged. This tests whether averaging calibrated scores beats averaging ranks.
backlog.title: Geometric-mean probability averaging instead of rank average

backlog.spec: Build on the current train.py after adopting the two changes that already beat noise: standardize molecules inside featurize (keep the largest fragment with rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser, neutralize with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger, fall back to the original molecule on failure), and add two rank-averaged members, a Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour scorer on binary Morgan bits (k=15) and an MLPClassifier((256,64), early_stopping=True) on QuantileTransformer-scaled features. The experiment: this benchmark is roughly 75/25 imbalanced, so give the minority class its due in every member. Set class_weight='balanced' on the RandomForest, scale_pos_weight (or class_weight) equivalently on LightGBM, auto_class_weights='Balanced' on CatBoost, and for the MLP pass per-sample weights by oversampling the minority class to parity with a seeded RandomOverSampler-style index resample built with numpy (no imblearn available). Leave the kNN member unweighted. Keep the equal-weight rank-average blend, the feature pipeline and the seed plumbing otherwise unchanged, so the only variable is class weighting.
backlog.title: Balanced class weights across every ensemble member

backlog.spec: On top of the current ensemble, change CatBoost to depth 4, l2_leaf_reg 10, iterations 800, learning_rate 0.03, rsm 0.2. Change LightGBM to num_leaves 8, min_child_samples 20, reg_lambda 5, n_estimators 500, learning_rate 0.03, colsample_bytree 0.3. Keep the RF unchanged and the rank average.
backlog.title: Shallow regularized CatBoost and LightGBM

backlog.spec: Add a fourth member: a CatBoostRegressor (depth 6, 500 iterations, lr 0.05, rsm 0.2) trained with RMSE on y mapped to 0/1 after label smoothing (0.05/0.95). Rank-average its predictions with the other three members.
backlog.title: CatBoost regressor on rank target

backlog.spec: In featurize(), add a small block of extra features per molecule: AllChem.ComputeGasteigerCharges(m) followed by summary statistics of the partial charges (max, min, sum of absolute values, and count of atoms with |charge|>0.3), plus counts of each Crippen atom type from rdMolDescriptors._CalcCrippenContribs(m) grouped by the type label (top 20 most frequent types across the training set, fixed at fit time). Append these to the existing descriptor and Morgan columns. Keep all models unchanged.
backlog.title: Gasteiger charge and Crippen atom-type count features

backlog.spec: Replace the LightGBM member with LGBMClassifier(boosting_type='dart', n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.08, num_leaves=15, extra_trees=True, drop_rate=0.1, colsample_bytree=0.3, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1). Keep the rank average.
backlog.title: Seeded LightGBM DART with extra trees

backlog.spec: Keep the ensemble structure as it is but retune the CatBoost member toward a shallower, more regularized model, since the dataset is small (about 1300 training molecules per fold) and folds test unseen scaffolds. Replace CatBoostClassifier(iterations=500, learning_rate=0.05, depth=6, rsm=0.2) with CatBoostClassifier(iterations=900, learning_rate=0.03, depth=4, l2_leaf_reg=8, rsm=0.15, bagging_temperature=1.0, thread_count=8, random_seed=seed, verbose=0). Change nothing else: same features, same other two members, same rank-average. Report the loss so the depth/regularization direction can be read off cleanly.
backlog.title: Shallow, strongly regularized CatBoost in the ensemble

backlog.spec: Change only the CatBoostClassifier in fit_predict so it uses bootstrap_type='Bayesian' with bagging_temperature=1.0, in place of the default Bayesian setting. Keep depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, iterations=500, rsm=0.2, thread_count=8 and random_seed=seed. Leave the other members and the rank average unchanged.
backlog.title: CatBoost with Bayesian bootstrap

backlog.spec: After the first ensemble pass, take the test molecules whose rank-averaged probability is in the top 25% or bottom 25% and which all three models agree on. Add them with hard labels to the training set. Refit all models and return the rank average of the refit predictions. Use only the seed argument for randomness.
backlog.title: Pseudo-label self-training

backlog.spec: Start from the current train.py and first adopt the two changes that already beat noise: (a) in featurize, standardize each molecule before featurizing by keeping the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser) and neutralizing charges (rdMolStandardize.Uncharger), falling back to the original molecule if standardization raises; (b) add two extra rank-averaged members, a Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour scorer on binary Morgan bits (k=15, score = mean Tanimoto similarity to the positive neighbours among the k nearest, or similarity-weighted mean of their labels) and an MLPClassifier (hidden_layer_sizes=(256,64), early_stopping=True) on QuantileTransformer-scaled features. Then the actual experiment: make the two gradient boosters shallower and much more regularized, since 1624 molecules with scaffold-disjoint folds favour high bias. Set LightGBM to num_leaves=15, max_depth=4, min_child_samples=30, learning_rate=0.03, n_estimators=600, reg_lambda=5.0, colsample_bytree=0.2, subsample=0.7, subsample_freq=1; set CatBoost to depth=4, iterations=800, learning_rate=0.03, l2_leaf_reg=10, rsm=0.15. Keep the rank-average blend (equal weights over the five members) and the seed plumbing unchanged. Report whether the regularized boosters help on top of the adopted base.
backlog.title: Shallow, strongly regularized boosters in the 5-member ensemble

backlog.spec: Before computing features, preprocess each SMILES: parse it, take the largest fragment, neutralize with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger, then canonicalize tautomers with rdMolStandardize.TautomerEnumerator().Canonicalize(m) inside a try/except that falls back to the previous molecule on failure. Recompute the molecule from Chem.MolToSmiles(m, isomericSmiles=False) and parse it again before all RDKit calls. Leave the rest of the ensemble unchanged.
backlog.title: Tautomer-canonicalize and strip stereo before featurizing

backlog.spec: Keep the ensemble structure as it is but retune only the LightGBM member for a small, wide, highly collinear feature matrix. Replace LGBMClassifier(n_estimators=300, learning_rate=0.05, num_leaves=31, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.3) with LGBMClassifier(n_estimators=700, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15, min_child_samples=20, reg_lambda=5.0, subsample=0.7, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.2, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed, verbose=-1). Change nothing else: same features, same RF and CatBoost members, same rank-average of the three members.
backlog.title: Shallow, strongly regularized LightGBM in the ensemble

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule. Give each sample weight 1/sqrt(count of its scaffold in training), normalized to a mean of 1. Pass it as sample_weight to RF, LightGBM and CatBoost fit calls.
backlog.title: Scaffold-weighted samples

memo: Helped: only the slot 0 rank-average ensemble of RF, LightGBM and CatBoost on descriptors plus Morgan counts (0.1361 to 0.0942). Nothing else was accepted, yet several rejected ideas beat noise (sd about 0.0049): slot 15 kNN plus MLP (0.0868 and 0.0853 over 2 runs, -0.0081), slot 12 largest fragment plus neutralization (0.0899, -0.0043), slot 24 (0.0904), slot 26 weighted five-member blend (0.0901). Adopt these. Not helpful: fingerprint additions (atom-pair, path, MACCS, FCFP, EState), stacking, extra tree/SVC/HGB members, RF tweaks, monotone constraints, seed bagging (all within about ±0.002). Hurt: physchem-only (+0.0381), descriptors-only RF (+0.0152), single CatBoost (+0.0079), per-view RFs (+0.0032), dropping rare columns (+0.0029), logistic regression blend (+0.0137). Next: make slot 15 the base, add slot 12 standardization, then replicate. Then tune CatBoost/LightGBM depth and regularization. Avoid more stacking and fingerprint additions.
